pr_title: Fix proximity fade's `world_pos` is calculated incorrectly when in gl_compatibility
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/89942

OpenGL ndc's z range is-1.0 to 1.0 by default while the Vulkan is 0.0 to 1.0.

issue_context.title: Proximity Fade broken in Compatibility (OpenGL)
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- v4.3.dev5.official [89f70e98d]

### System information

Godot v4.3.dev5 - macOS 13.6.0 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - Apple M1 Pro - Apple M1 Pro (8 Threads)

### Issue description

The Proximity Fade in StandardMaterial3D does not work with Compatibility renderer. The produced code assumes Vulkan Z range 0.0 to 1.0 instead of OpenGL -1.0 to 1.0. The fix is to remap the depth_tex as follows:

```glsl
// Proximity Fade: Enabled
	float depth_tex = textureLod(depth_texture, SCREEN_UV, 0.0).r;
        depth_tex = depth_tex * 2.0 - 1.0; // <-- For OpenGL
	vec4 world_pos = INV_PROJECTION_MATRIX * vec4(SCREEN_UV * 2.0 - 1.0, depth_tex, 1.0);
	world_pos.xyz /= world_pos.w;
	ALPHA *= clamp(1.0 - smoothstep(world_pos.z + proximity_fade_distance, world_pos.z, VERTEX.z), 0.0, 1.0);
```

### Steps to reproduce

- Use Compatibility renderer.
- Add a cube on a plane, or two intersecting cubes, etc. 
- Apply a new standardMaterial3D and enable Proximity Fade.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A

review_comments:
Could we make this part be introduced by the shader preprocessor, instead of a C++ condition? This way, if you convert the BaseMaterial3D to a ShaderMaterial (making its shader code fixed), it'll keep working if you switch rendering methods afterwards. This is also important to handle situations where a project can [fall back to Compatibility if Vulkan isn't supported](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8006).

(Also, I thought we already had automatic depth correction when using the Compatibility rendering method, so we wouldn't have to do this.)

Indeed it would be great if the depth_texture was driver agnostic, so the same shader code would work regardless of renderer. Or a preprocessor macro that converts it into 0-1 (and does nothing if Vulkan).

I'm sorry for my previous explaination of this problem, let me put it more clearly: depth is 0-1 but the ndc is different in opengl and vulkan. It's introduced in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/54285, it changed to vulkan way of ndc so it caused this issue.

Visual shader also use an if here, see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/74910. But we'd better not use this approach as Calinou mentioned.
In 4.4+ we now have a way to do this with preprocessor defines. I made a PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100220.

> In 4.4+ we now have a way to do this with preprocessor defines. I made a PR: #100220.

Seems pretty reasonable. Closing this pr now.

Your approach may still end up being the right one, actually. It looks like preprocessor macros don't quite work right now in the generated shaders in materials. We'll see if that ends up being considered a bug or not.

> It looks like preprocessor macros don't quite work right now in the generated shaders in materials.

I suppose this can be tweaked a little? Not sure it's a bug or not, but worth investigating.
